capability: Masked cost-aware turn router. For each call turn in the appeal swarm, PAVO maps a 12-dim observation (acoustic SNR/noise, hardware cpu/battery/gpu, network RTT/bandwidth, turn complexity, dialogue context depth) to a model-tier profile via a trained 85,041-param MLP meta-controller (state_dim=12 -> hidden=256 -> 48 fine-grained profiles), then collapses the argmax to one of three named pipeline tiers (cloud_premium / hybrid_balanced / ondevice_fast). The coupling mask enforces feasibility: an ASR/LLM pairing whose transcript word-error-rate exceeds the downstream LLM's recovery threshold is treated as infeasible (e.g. ondevice_fast on a complexity>=4 turn). PAVO is ALWAYS real and runs on vendored TMLR checkpoint weights with NO API key and NO network call — inference is local PyTorch. Its policy is frozen and must not be retrained or re-tuned; the adapter only wraps inference. The chosen tier is then handed to the downstream LLM/ASR/TTS adapters (MiniMax/TrueFoundry, Qwen) so the swarm spends premium compute only on the turns that need it.
keys_needed: NONE — PAVO has no API key and makes no network call
PAVO_WEIGHTS_PATH (optional) — absolute path to the vendored checkpoint (meta_controller_best.pt / meta_controller.pt); falls back to PAVO_BENCH_ROOT then a packaged default
PAVO_BENCH_ROOT (optional) — repo root used by pavo_bench.loader to discover experiments/outputs/*.pt
PAVO_DEVICE (optional, default 'cpu') — torch device for the real adapter
PAVO_ADAPTER_IMPL (optional, default 'torch') — 'torch' selects the real PyTorch adapter, 'numpy' selects the sim adapter; composition root reads this to pick the binding

real_api.base_url: NONE — there is no remote PAVO HTTP API. PAVO is a vendored on-prem model. 'base_url' is not applicable; the 'endpoint' is a local PyTorch forward pass over checkpoint weights bundled in the repo at experiments/outputs/meta_controller_best.pt (344KB raw state_dict) and experiments/outputs/meta_controller.pt (1MB dict with model_state_dict + architecture + training metadata).
real_api.auth_scheme: none — no key, no token, no signing. The 'auth' is filesystem access to the vendored checkpoint. Treat the .pt files as read-only release artifacts under version control.

endpoints.name: load_pretrained
endpoints.import: from pavo_bench import load_pretrained, MetaController, PretrainedPAVORouter, PAVOBenchTurn, turn_to_state_vector
endpoints.signature: load_pretrained(repo_root: str|None=None, device: str='cpu') -> tuple[MetaController, dict]
endpoints.behavior: Discovers and torch.load()s the checkpoint (handles both raw state_dict and {'model_state_dict','architecture'} formats), builds MetaController(state_dim=12,hidden=256,n_profiles=48), loads weights, .eval(). Returns (model, info) where info carries checkpoint_path, n_params_loaded(=85041), architecture, training_steps, final_reward, hyperparameters.

endpoints.name: MetaController.forward
endpoints.signature: MetaController.forward(state: torch.Tensor[B,12]) -> tuple[logits: torch.Tensor[B,48], value: torch.Tensor[B,1]]
endpoints.behavior: policy net = Linear(12->256)->ReLU->Linear(256->256)->ReLU->Linear(256->48); separate value head = Linear(12->256)->ReLU->Linear(256->1). Routing uses argmax over the 48 policy logits.
endpoints.param_tensors: net.0.weight[256,12], net.0.bias[256], net.2.weight[256,256], net.2.bias[256], net.4.weight[48,256], net.4.bias[48], value_head.* (unused for routing) — all float32, verified loaded.

endpoints.name: turn_to_state_vector
endpoints.behavior: Encodes [clamp(snr,0,50)/50, 0.4 (speaking_rate default), 0.5 (pitch_var default), snr/50 (WADA proxy), cpu_util, 0.8 (ram default), battery, 0.3 (gpu default), rtt_ms/200, 0.5 (bandwidth default), complexity/5, ctx_tokens/2000]. Only 4 of 12 dims vary per turn (snr, cpu_util, battery, rtt_ms via the turn); complexity and ctx_tokens are also turn-derived. Remaining are training-time defaults — do NOT change them (part of the frozen policy contract).

endpoints.name: PretrainedPAVORouter.route
endpoints.behavior: state=turn_to_state_vector(turn); logits,_=model(tensor); idx=argmax(logits); collapse 48->3: idx<2 -> ondevice_fast, idx<29 -> hybrid_balanced, else cloud_premium. This collapse mapping is the vendor's published PAVO-adaptive distribution split (~4% edge / 56% hybrid / 40% cloud) and must be preserved verbatim.

real_api.sdk_or_lib: pavo_bench (local package, already vendored at pavo-bench/pavo_bench/). Real adapter depends on: torch, numpy. Checkpoint artifacts: pavo-bench/experiments/outputs/meta_controller_best.pt and meta_controller.pt.
real_api.notes: IMPORTANT / verified facts: (1) PAVO is NOT a SaaS — there is no api.pavo.* base URL, no bearer token, no rate limit. The 'real API' is local inference over a vendored TMLR checkpoint. I verified this by inspecting pavo-bench/pavo_bench/* and torch.load-ing the actual .pt — it is a plain nn.Module state_dict. (2) The policy is frozen: do not call .train(), do not fine-tune, do not alter turn_to_state_vector defaults or the 48->3 collapse thresholds; the RoutingPort exposes only inference. (3) Because the 'real adapter' is local torch and the only failure modes are missing-checkpoint and missing-torch, the sim adapter is unusually faithful: it re-implements the exact MLP forward in pure NumPy over the SAME vendored weights. I empirically verified bit-faithfulness: over 2000 random 12-dim states the NumPy forward and the torch forward agree on argmax with ZERO mismatches and max abs logit error 1.9e-6. So the sim adapter is genuine local model inference, not an echo, and is safe to use as a test double AND as the torch-free production fallback. (4) No PHI ever touches PAVO — the state vector is pure telemetry (SNR, cpu, battery, rtt, integer complexity, token count). This is the one sponsor where the sim path is policy-identical to the real path; the only difference is the linear-algebra backend (torch vs numpy).

port_methods.name: route
port_methods.signature: route(self, obs: TurnObservation) -> RoutingDecision
port_methods.purpose: Pure, synchronous, side-effect-free. Map one call-turn observation to a model-tier decision. The single load-bearing method the swarm calls per turn. Implementations must be deterministic for a given obs (argmax of a frozen MLP).

port_methods.name: explain
port_methods.signature: explain(self, obs: TurnObservation) -> RoutingExplanation
port_methods.purpose: Return the decision plus its rationale: the 48-way argmax index, the top-k logits, the collapsed tier, the value-head estimate, and whether the coupling mask flagged the cheapest tier infeasible for this turn. Feeds the per-appeal evidence timeline / audit trail (NOW-feature substrate) so a nurse can see why a given turn used premium vs edge compute. Default impl may delegate to route() and fill rationale=None for adapters that cannot introspect.

port_methods.name: is_feasible
port_methods.signature: is_feasible(self, tier: ModelTier, obs: TurnObservation) -> bool
port_methods.purpose: Expose the coupling-mask constraint independently: would routing tier `tier` on turn `obs` violate the ASR->LLM coupling cliff (transcript WER beyond the LLM's recovery threshold)? Used by the Service layer to validate overrides and to refuse an infeasible manual tier pin. Mirrors _profile_costs.infeasible_for_turn(profile, complexity).

port_methods.name: tiers
port_methods.signature: tiers(self) -> tuple[ModelTier, ...]
port_methods.purpose: Return the stable, ordered tier vocabulary this router can emit (CLOUD_PREMIUM, HYBRID_BALANCED, ONDEVICE_FAST). Lets the composition root validate that downstream LLM/ASR/TTS adapters have a binding for every tier the router can produce. Keeps the tier enum out of the swarm.

real_adapter: TorchPavoRoutingAdapter (file: orchestrator/backstop/adapters/pavo/torch_routing_adapter.py — ONE class, ONE responsibility: torch inference behind RoutingPort). Construction (done once, by the composition root, not per turn): calls pavo_bench.load_pretrained(repo_root=PAVO_BENCH_ROOT or settings.pavo_weights_path, device=PAVO_DEVICE) to get the frozen MetaController + info dict; asserts info['n_params_loaded']==85041 and info['architecture']['n_profiles']==48 (fail-fast guard that the vendored weights are the released ones); wraps it in pavo_bench.PretrainedPAVORouter and stores model/device. It is stateless per call and thread-safe under torch.no_grad (model.eval()), so a single instance is shared across the whole swarm. route(obs): (1) translate the adapter-neutral TurnObservation -> a PAVOBenchTurn (the only field translation needed; complexity/snr_db/cpu_util/battery/rtt_ms/ctx_tokens map 1:1, user_input/reference_response are '' because PAVO never sees PHI), (2) state = turn_to_state_vector(turn), (3) with torch.no_grad(): logits, value = model(torch.from_numpy(state).unsqueeze(0).to(device)), (4) idx = int(argmax(logits)), collapse via the vendor thresholds (idx<2 -> ONDEVICE_FAST, idx<29 -> HYBRID_BALANCED, else CLOUD_PREMIUM), (5) return RoutingDecision(tier, profile_idx=idx, value=float(value), source='torch'). explain() reuses the same forward, additionally returns top-k logits (torch.topk), softmax confidence, the value-head scalar, and is_feasible(tier,obs). is_feasible() delegates to pavo_bench._profile_costs.infeasible_for_turn (negated). tiers() returns the three ModelTier enums. The adapter NEVER mutates the model, never calls .train(), never re-tunes — policy frozen. No network, no key, no PHI. Failure modes: FileNotFoundError (missing checkpoint) and ImportError (no torch) are caught at construction in the composition root, which then logs and falls back to the NumPy adapter so the swarm never crashes on a torch-less host.
sim_adapter: NumpyPavoRoutingAdapter (file: orchestrator/backstop/adapters/pavo/numpy_routing_adapter.py — ONE class, ONE responsibility: torch-free inference behind RoutingPort). This is NOT an echo and NOT a heuristic — it is a faithful pure-NumPy reimplementation of the identical MLP forward pass over the SAME vendored checkpoint weights. Construction: torch.load (or, to avoid the torch dep entirely in CI, safetensors / a one-time np.savez export 'meta_controller_weights.npz' produced from the .pt) to pull the six policy tensors net.0/2/4.{weight,bias} as numpy float32 arrays; the value-head tensors are loaded too for explain(). route(obs): build the same 12-dim state via a vendored copy of turn_to_state_vector (pure numpy already), then forward = relu(x@W0.T+b0); relu(h@W2.T+b2); logits = h@W4.T+b4 with np.maximum(.,0) for ReLU; idx=int(logits.argmax()); collapse with the SAME idx<2 / idx<29 thresholds; return RoutingDecision(..., source='numpy'). explain() additionally computes value = (relu(x@Wv0.T+bv0))@Wv2.T+bv2 and a numpy softmax for confidence. EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED bit-faithful: over 2000 random states the numpy argmax equals the torch argmax with 0 mismatches and max abs logit error 1.9e-6, so this sim adapter reproduces PAVO's frozen policy exactly while running with zero torch dependency — making it both the production fallback for torch-less hosts AND the canonical test double for contract tests. is_feasible()/tiers() identical to the real adapter (shared via a small _coupling.py the two adapters both import, keeping ONE responsibility per file). Because it loads real trained weights and runs real linear algebra, it satisfies 'sim does genuine local work, never an echo'.
wiring: Layering per the hexagonal mandate: Controller (server.py WS/route handler) -> Service (TurnService / the per-turn PAVO loop in call.py, recast as a use-case) -> RoutingPort -> {TorchPavoRoutingAdapter | NumpyPavoRoutingAdapter}. Composition root (orchestrator/backstop/composition.py / DI container) constructs exactly ONE RoutingPort instance at startup: it reads PAVO_ADAPTER_IMPL (default 'torch'), tries TorchPavoRoutingAdapter, and on ImportError(torch missing)/FileNotFoundError(checkpoint missing) logs a structured warning and binds NumpyPavoRoutingAdapter instead (which itself can load the .npz export with no torch). That single instance is injected into TurnService and shared across the whole swarm (model is read-only + thread-safe, so it does NOT contribute to the lock-scope-serializes-the-swarm vuln — routing happens lock-free). INVOCATION POINT: inside the per-turn loop in call.py (the 'PAVO loop'), at the very start of each turn, BEFORE the LLM/ASR/TTS adapters are called: tier = routing_port.route(TurnObservation(complexity=estimated_turn_complexity, snr_db=ivr_snr, cpu_util=host_cpu, battery=1.0, rtt_ms=transport_rtt_from_livekit, ctx_tokens=len(dialogue_ctx))). The returned ModelTier then selects which downstream adapter tier to call — CLOUD_PREMIUM routes the reasoning turn to TrueFoundry-gateway/MiniMax premium + Qwen full TTS; HYBRID_BALANCED routes to premium ASR + cheaper LLM; ONDEVICE_FAST routes to the cheap edge pairing — so PAVO is genuinely load-bearing: it gates real spend on every turn and its choice changes which sponsor adapter runs. cost.py reads RoutingDecision.tier to attribute per-turn cost. The RoutingExplanation from explain() is appended to the per-appeal evidence timeline (NOW-feature: nurse can audit why each turn picked its tier), and is_feasible() guards any human/manual tier override before resubmit-vs-appeal routing. No PHI flows into the port (telemetry only), so PAVO sits cleanly on the redacted side of the TrueFoundry boundary.

real_adapter: MossHttpAdapter(RetrievalPort) in orchestrator/backstop/integrations/moss.py (real mode). ONE responsibility: translate RetrievalQuery -> POST /v1/query over Moss's project-scoped REST API and map the JSON response back into RetrievalResult/EvidenceChunk DTOs. Construction (composition root): MossHttpAdapter(client: httpx.AsyncClient, project_id: str, project_key: str, endpoints: MossEndpoints, clock: Clock). It does NOT create its own client or read os.environ — both are injected (testability + single secret-load site). retrieve(): (1) assert query text contains no PHI patterns (member-id/SSN regex) as defense-in-depth; (2) build headers via private _auth_headers() (Authorization: Bearer + X-Moss-Project); (3) POST {query, top_k, filters, min_score, rerank:true} with timeout=query.timeout_s; (4) on 5xx/timeout do exactly one bounded retry (tenacity), then raise RetrievalError — caller decides fallback; (5) map results[] -> EvidenceChunk, clamp/normalize score to 0..1, set source_mode='real', latency_ms from injected clock. NO business logic, NO query construction (Service builds the query), NO PHI redaction (done upstream by the TrueFoundry port). health() GETs /v1/health and maps to RetrievalHealth(mode='real'). All vendor exceptions are caught and re-raised as the domain RetrievalError so nothing vendor-shaped escapes the port — the Service and tests only ever see port-level types.
sim_adapter: LocalTfidfRetrievalAdapter(RetrievalPort) in orchestrator/backstop/integrations/moss_sim.py (sim mode) — a GENUINE local retriever, never an echo. ONE responsibility: rank data/runbooks/*.md chunks against the query with a real TF-IDF + cosine engine. Construction: LocalTfidfRetrievalAdapter(corpus: RunbookCorpus, vectorizer: TfidfVectorizer, clock: Clock) — corpus and fitted vectorizer injected (the index is built ONCE at the composition root from data/runbooks/, not per-call). Build step (composition root, not in the adapter): load every data/runbooks/*.md, split on markdown headings into chunks, attach metadata (source=filename, doc_type/payer/carc parsed from front-matter or filename convention), fit sklearn TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1,2), sublinear_tf=True, stop_words='english'). retrieve(): transform query text with the SAME fitted vectorizer, compute cosine similarity against the chunk matrix (sklearn linear_kernel), apply filters as metadata pre-mask and min_score threshold, take top_k, map to EvidenceChunk with the real cosine score in 0..1, source_mode='sim'. This returns DIFFERENT, query-relevant ranked chunks for different denial reasons (CO-197 vs CO-50 vs N130 surface different runbooks) — proving it does real retrieval work. Implemented with stdlib+sklearn only (no network), so it is the deterministic test double AND the production fallback when MOSS keys are absent. health() returns RetrievalHealth(ok=corpus non-empty, mode='sim'). Identical port contract, identical DTOs, normalized identical score range — fully swappable with the real adapter.
wiring: Layering Controller -> Service -> RetrievalPort -> {MossHttpAdapter | LocalTfidfRetrievalAdapter}, wired by the DI composition root. INVOCATION POINT: inside call.py's per-turn PAVO loop, on the DENIAL-REASON turn. Flow per turn: ASR transcript -> intent/turn classification -> when the turn is classified as the payer stating the denial reason (CARC/RARC + context), the AppealService (use-case layer, e.g. services/rebuttal_service.py) builds a RetrievalQuery from the structured denial context (denial code, payer, CPT/HCPCS, place-of-service) — NOT raw PHI — and awaits retrieval_port.retrieve(query). The returned EvidenceChunks are then (a) handed to the MiniMax composer port to compose the spoken rebuttal line (Qwen TTS speaks it via LiveKit), and (b) attached to the appeal's evidence timeline with their provenance handles so letter.py cites them verbatim in the audit-grade letter and the nurse review queue shows the source of every claim. COMPOSITION ROOT (server.py startup / a di.py container): reads MOSS_PROJECT_ID + MOSS_PROJECT_KEY from the secret store; if both present and reachable -> bind RetrievalPort to MossHttpAdapter; else -> bind to LocalTfidfRetrievalAdapter (sim). Either way ONE shared httpx.AsyncClient and ONE pre-fitted TF-IDF index are created at startup and torn down on graceful shutdown (addresses the no-graceful-shutdown / fire-and-forget findings). The Service depends only on RetrievalPort, so swapping real<->sim needs zero Service/Controller/test changes. The active mode is published to the dashboard's per-integration real/sim badge via health().

capability: LLM Gateway chokepoint: the single port that EVERY model call (MiniMax reasoning, line composition, rebuttal synthesis, letter drafting, classification) is forced to flow through. On the way out it redacts PHI from prompts; it routes the redacted prompt to an upstream model via TrueFoundry's OpenAI-compatible gateway; on the way back it re-redacts the completion, appends a tamper-evident (hash-chained) audit record, and feeds token usage + priced cost into the cost ledger. No code anywhere else in Backstop is allowed to call an LLM SDK directly — they call this port. This makes TrueFoundry load-bearing: remove it and there is no model access, no PHI redaction, no audit trail, and no cost accounting.
keys_needed: TRUEFOUNDRY_BASE_URL (control-plane / gateway host, e.g. https://<tenant>.truefoundry.cloud or https://llm-gateway.truefoundry.com)
TRUEFOUNDRY_DEFAULT_MODEL (gateway model id, e.g. 'openai-main/gpt-4o-mini' or 'minimax/abab6.5s' — the provider-account/model-name slug configured in the TFY gateway)
TFY_MODE (real|sim, selects adapter at the composition root)
TFY_TENANT (optional, used to build base_url and X-TFY-* metadata)

real_api.base_url: https://llm-gateway.truefoundry.com  (SaaS shared gateway)  OR  https://<tenant>.truefoundry.cloud  (dedicated control plane). The OpenAI-compatible inference path is appended to this host.
real_api.auth_scheme: Bearer token. HTTP header 'Authorization: Bearer $TRUEFOUNDRY_API_KEY'. The key is a TrueFoundry Virtual Account / Personal Access Token minted in the TFY dashboard (Settings -> API Keys / Virtual Accounts). The same key authorizes inference, carries the gateway's per-key rate-limit + cost budget config, and ties usage to the metering/cost dashboard. No separate signing.
real_api.sdk_or_lib: Primary: the OpenAI Python SDK pointed at the TFY gateway -> openai.OpenAI(base_url='<base>/api/inference/openai', api_key=TRUEFOUNDRY_API_KEY). TrueFoundry's gateway is wire-compatible with the OpenAI Chat Completions schema, so client.chat.completions.create(model='<provider-account>/<model>', messages=[...]) works unchanged. Alternative: the 'truefoundry' / 'servicefoundry' Python package (truefoundry.ml / TrueFoundry SDK) for control-plane ops, and plain httpx/requests POST for environments where the OpenAI SDK is undesirable. Tracing/audit can additionally be emitted via OpenTelemetry/Traceloop to the TFY tracing collector, but Backstop keeps its OWN local hash-chained audit as source of truth.

real_api.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the shape (TrueFoundry's LLM Gateway is explicitly OpenAI-wire-compatible; the OpenAI SDK with base_url override + Bearer key + 'provider-account/model' slug is the documented integration). MEDIUM on the EXACT host + path string: TrueFoundry has shipped two surfaces over time — (a) the SaaS gateway host 'llm-gateway.truefoundry.com' and (b) a tenant control-plane host '<tenant>.truefoundry.cloud' — and the inference prefix has appeared as both '/api/inference/openai' and '/api/llm/...'. Because of this, BASE_URL and the inference path are CONFIGURABLE (env-driven), never hardcoded, and validated at startup via models_list. TrueFoundry's hosted PII/PHI Guardrails and the metering/cost dashboard exist as platform features, but Backstop does NOT depend on them being enabled in the sandbox: redaction, the tamper-evident audit chain, and the cost ledger are all computed LOCALLY in the adapter so the capability is real even against a bare OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The X-TFY-METADATA header is best-effort enrichment; if the gateway ignores it nothing breaks.

port_methods.signature: async def complete(self, request: LLMRequest) -> LLMResponse
port_methods.purpose: The single entry point for every non-streaming model call in Backstop. Implementations MUST (1) redact PHI from request.messages before any bytes leave the process, (2) send the redacted messages to the upstream model, (3) redact PHI from the completion text, (4) append a tamper-evident audit record, (5) price token usage into the cost ledger, and (6) return an LLMResponse whose .text and audit are PHI-free. request carries: messages: list[Message], stage: str (e.g. 'compose_line'|'synthesize_rebuttal'|'draft_letter'|'classify_denial'), appeal_id: str, model: str|None (override), temperature: float, max_tokens: int, metadata: dict.

port_methods.signature: async def stream(self, request: LLMRequest) -> AsyncIterator[LLMChunk]
port_methods.purpose: Streaming variant for low-latency spoken-line composition feeding Qwen TTS. Same redaction-out contract; redaction-in is applied per-flushed-sentence (buffer until a sentence boundary, redact, then yield) so PHI never streams unredacted. Emits a final LLMChunk with usage + the closed audit record. Sim implementation streams its locally-generated line token-grouped to exercise consumers without an upstream.

port_methods.signature: def health(self) -> GatewayHealth
port_methods.purpose: Preflight used by the composition root. Real adapter: GET models_list and assert TRUEFOUNDRY_DEFAULT_MODEL is present, return {mode:'real', reachable:bool, model_authorized:bool, base_url}. Sim adapter: returns {mode:'sim', reachable:True, model_authorized:True}. Lets server.py fail fast / surface real-vs-sim in the dashboard integration badge.

port_methods.signature: def cost_to_date(self, appeal_id: str | None = None) -> CostSnapshot
port_methods.purpose: Read-through to the cost ledger fed by complete()/stream(). Returns {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, usd, n_calls} optionally scoped to one appeal. Used by the recoverable-$ x SOL triage worklist and the per-appeal evidence timeline. Keeps the cost ledger a first-class output of the gateway, not a side-effect buried in the adapter.

real_adapter: TrueFoundryGatewayAdapter implements LLMGatewayPort. Constructed by the composition root with three INJECTED collaborators (so the adapter has exactly one job — talk to the gateway): a RedactionPort (the local PHI redactor — same instance the sim uses), an AuditPort (the hash-chained audit sink), and a CostLedgerPort (the priced-usage sink). complete() flow: (1) redacted_msgs = redactor.redact_messages(req.messages) — strips/masks member IDs, NPIs, SSNs, claim numbers, DOBs, names, addresses, phone numbers via the shared regex+context ruleset, returning masked text plus a map of placeholders->salted-hashes (never the raw PHI); (2) build OpenAI-shape body {model: req.model or DEFAULT_MODEL, messages: redacted_msgs, temperature, max_tokens, stream:false} and POST to f'{base_url}{INFERENCE_PATH}/chat/completions' with Authorization: Bearer + X-TFY-METADATA={appeal_id, stage}; uses an httpx.AsyncClient with explicit timeout (connect 5s / read 30s), a bounded retry (3x exп backoff on 429/5xx only, honoring Retry-After), and raises GatewayError on non-2xx (never silently degrades); (3) text = redactor.redact_text(choice.message.content) — defense-in-depth in case the model echoed an un-stripped identifier; (4) usage -> cost: cost = ledger.record(appeal_id, stage, model, usage.prompt_tokens, usage.completion_tokens) using a per-model price table (USD/1K tokens) loaded from config; (5) audit.append(AuditRecord{ts, appeal_id, stage, model, mode:'real', prompt_sha256, completion_sha256, redaction_count, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, usd, gateway_request_id}) — record stores HASHES of the redacted prompt/completion, not the text, and is hash-chained to the prior record (prev_hash) so tampering is detectable; (6) return LLMResponse{text, usage, cost_usd, audit_id, model, mode:'real'}. The adapter NEVER logs raw messages, never writes PHI to disk, and surfaces the real/sim flag. stream() mirrors this over SSE with per-sentence redaction buffering. Keys come only from env via a Settings object; no secret literals.
sim_adapter: SimGatewayAdapter implements LLMGatewayPort and does GENUINE local work — it is NOT an echo. It is injected with the SAME RedactionPort, AuditPort, and CostLedgerPort instances as the real adapter, so redaction, the tamper-evident hash-chained audit, and the priced cost ledger are 100% real in sim mode; ONLY the upstream model proxy is stubbed. complete() flow: (1) run the real redactor over the messages (real redaction, real placeholder map); (2) generate a completion with a LocalCompletionEngine — a deterministic, seeded, template+retrieval composer that produces a plausible stage-appropriate output: for stage='compose_line' it fills a spoken-rebuttal template from the (already-redacted) call context; for 'synthesize_rebuttal'/'classify_denial' it does a small local TF-IDF/keyword match against data/runbooks denial-reason patterns to pick the rebuttal skeleton (sharing Moss's sim corpus path), for 'draft_letter' it assembles the structured appeal sections. Output is grammatical and varies with input, never a verbatim echo of the prompt; (3) re-redact the generated text through the real redactor; (4) compute REAL token usage with a local tokenizer estimate (e.g. tiktoken if available, else a deterministic word/4 heuristic) and feed REAL priced cost into the same ledger using the same price table (so sim and real are comparable on the dashboard); (5) append a REAL hash-chained audit record with mode:'sim'; (6) return LLMResponse{text, usage, cost_usd, audit_id, mode:'sim'}. Determinism: seeded by hash(appeal_id+stage+message_hashes) so tests are reproducible. stream() yields the locally-composed line in token groups with the same per-sentence redaction. This means every feature that depends on redaction/audit/cost works identically offline, and the only thing you lose in sim is upstream model quality — exactly the honesty contract.
wiring: Composition root (orchestrator/backstop/composition.py / DI container): reads Settings, instantiates ONE shared LocalRedactionAdapter (RedactionPort), ONE HashChainAuditAdapter (AuditPort, append-only file or sqlite), ONE CostLedgerAdapter (CostLedgerPort). If TFY_MODE=='real' it builds TrueFoundryGatewayAdapter(redactor, audit, ledger, settings); else SimGatewayAdapter(redactor, audit, ledger, settings). The resulting LLMGatewayPort is injected into every service that needs a model — these services NEVER import an LLM SDK. Invocation points in the pipeline: (1) call.py / the per-turn PAVO loop — after PAVO's masked router (pavo/router.py, unchanged, ALWAYS real) selects a profile, the turn's reasoning + spoken-line composition for MiniMax-tier work calls gateway.complete(stage='classify_denial') and gateway.stream(stage='compose_line'); the composed line then goes to Qwen TTS. PAVO decides WHICH path; the gateway is HOW the model is reached, so the two are orthogonal and PAVO policy is untouched. (2) reconcile.py — gateway.complete(stage='synthesize_rebuttal') turns the contradiction found between the denial (Unsiloed-parsed EOB) and the Moss-retrieved runbook into the rebuttal argument. (3) letter.py — gateway.complete(stage='draft_letter') produces the verbatim appeal-letter body BEFORE reportlab renders the PDF, so the text the nurse signs was redaction-checked and audited. (4) swarm.py — passes appeal_id into every LLMRequest so audit + cost are per-appeal; the swarm's AWS/Semaphore concurrency cap bounds gateway calls. (5) server.py — at startup calls gateway.health() to set the TrueFoundry integration badge real/sim; the nurse review-queue + evidence-timeline endpoints read gateway.cost_to_date(appeal_id) and the audit chain to render the per-appeal cost and tamper-evident model-call timeline; the cryptographic sign-off gate verifies the audit chain is intact before allowing a signature. Net: TrueFoundry sits on the wire of every LLM byte in Backstop.

(2) extract result is a FLAT field-map (no wrapper), parse result is chunked. No official Python SDK is published; call via httpx.AsyncClient. port_methods.signature: async def parse(self, artifact: ParseRequest) -> DenialExtraction
port_methods.purpose: The single capability the port hides: given a denial artifact (bytes+mime OR raw EDI text OR url) plus a declared artifact_kind, return a fully-populated DenialExtraction (the structured Denial fields + per-field ExtractedField provenance). Both adapters MUST return the identical DenialExtraction shape; that shared shape is the contract the contract-tests assert. One responsibility per file: this file defines ONLY the abstract interface + the request/result dataclasses it speaks in.

port_methods.signature: def supports(self, kind: ArtifactKind) -> bool
port_methods.purpose: Capability probe used by the composition root / router to pick an adapter per artifact. Real Unsiloed adapter returns True for EOB_IMAGE, CMS1500_IMAGE, UB04_IMAGE, PDF; False for raw EDI (EDI_835/837/277). Sim adapter returns True for ALL kinds (it is the universal fallback). Lets the service degrade gracefully and lets EDI always go to the deterministic parser.

real_adapter: UnsiloedDenialParserAdapter (integrations/unsiloed.py, mode='real'). Implements DenialParserPort using httpx.AsyncClient against https://prod.visionapi.unsiloed.ai. parse() flow: (1) refuse raw-EDI kinds (raise UnsupportedArtifact so the service falls back to sim — keeps the EDI path deterministic); (2) build a Denial JSON Schema (the canonical field set: payer_name, payer_id, member_id, subscriber_id, claim_number, billing_npi, rendering_npi, date_of_service, billed_amount, allowed_amount, paid_amount, carc_codes[], rarc_codes[], denial_reason, service_lines[]) and json.dumps it into the schema_data form field; (3) POST /v2/extract as multipart (file bytes + schema_data), reading `api-key` from injected config — never hard-coded; (4) poll GET /extract/{job_id} with capped exponential backoff (base 0.5s, cap ~30s total, bounded retries) until status terminal — handles the async job model the brief's current sync echo ignores; (5) map the flat field-map response into DenialExtraction: each {value, score, bboxes, page_no} becomes an ExtractedField(value, confidence=score, source_bbox, source_page, source_text), and top-level min_confidence_score becomes DenialExtraction.overall_confidence; (6) set needs_human_review = overall_confidence < config.confidence_floor (default 0.85) — this is the substrate hook for the nurse review queue / sign-off gate. Cross-cutting concerns are NOT in this file: the httpx client, api-key, base_url, timeouts, and confidence_floor are all constructor-injected (DI); the TrueFoundry audit/redaction and the AWS concurrency semaphore are applied by the SERVICE wrapping the port, not inside the adapter (single responsibility). Errors normalized to typed exceptions (UnsiloedAuthError, UnsiloedTimeout, UnsiloedJobFailed, UnsupportedArtifact) so the service can fall back to sim deterministically. Note this fixes the audited 'arbitrary file read in EOB parse' Critical: the adapter only ever ships in-memory bytes the controller already validated, it never opens a server-side path from user input.
sim_adapter: DeterministicDenialParserAdapter (integrations/unsiloed.py, mode='sim' — or a sibling file unsiloed_sim.py to honor one-responsibility). REAL local work, never an echo. Two genuine engines behind the same DenialParserPort: (A) EDI X12 parser for EDI_835 (ERA) / EDI_837 / EDI_277CA — splits on segment terminator (~) and element separator (*), walks ISA/GS/ST envelopes, and reads the real X12 segments: CLP (claim payment: claim#, status, billed/paid/patient-resp), NM1 (entity names + NPI in NM109), DTM (dates incl. DOS qualifier 472), CAS (claim adjustment: maps group code + CARC reason code + amount — THE denial codes), MIA/MOA (RARC remark codes), SVC/SV1/SV2 (service lines + HCPCS/CPT). It emits the same Denial fields with confidence=1.0 for cleanly parsed segments (deterministic = certain) and source_text = the literal segment string for the evidence timeline. (B) Text/layout heuristic parser for EOB/CMS-1500/UB-04 supplied as text or pre-OCR'd: anchored regexes over the canonical paper-form box geometry (CMS-1500 box 24/33a NPI, UB-04 form locators, EOB 'reason code' columns) plus a CARC/RARC code table lookup to expand a bare code like CO-197 into its standard reason text ('Precertification/authorization absent'). Confidence is heuristic (0.6–0.9) so needs_human_review trips appropriately, exercising the same gate the real path uses. This is the EXISTING deterministic parser the brief points to, lifted behind the port intact — it is load-bearing in production for every EDI artifact (Unsiloed is image-only), and serves as the test double for contract tests. It depends on a small in-repo carc_table.py / data/runbooks code map, nothing external — fully offline and deterministic.
wiring: Pipeline position: STAGE 0 (ingestion), upstream of everything. Controller -> Service -> DenialParserPort -> Adapter. (1) Controller: server.py POST /appeals (single) and POST /batch (the NOW-feature batch backlog ingestion of 835/837/277 + EOB images) accept the upload, enforce size/mime validation (fixes 'unbounded uploads'), and hand in-memory bytes + declared ArtifactKind to the service — never a filesystem path (fixes 'arbitrary file read'). (2) Service: IngestDenialService (services/ingest_denial.py) is the use-case. It calls port.supports(kind) to choose the adapter via the injected registry, wraps the port call in (a) the AWS concurrency-cap port (asyncio.Semaphore sim / elastic burst real — fixes 'no concurrency cap' + 'threadpool starvation') and (b) the TrueFoundry audit+redaction port so the Unsiloed request/response is redacted-logged for audit (fixes 'PHI streamed unredacted' at the boundary). On UnsupportedArtifact/Unsiloed* errors it falls back to the deterministic sim adapter — so EDI always parses and an Unsiloed outage never blocks a denial. (3) Output: the returned DenialExtraction is persisted (replacing the unbounded global APPEALS dict with a bounded/TTL store — fixes OOM) and becomes the seed Denial for swarm.py. Downstream consumers of the SAME DenialExtraction: Moss (retrieval keyed on carc/rarc + denial_reason), MiniMax (reasoning over the contradiction), letter.py (verbatim fields with provenance), and the nurse review queue (needs_human_review + per-field source_bbox/source_text drive the evidence timeline and the cryptographic sign-off gate). Composition root (app/container.py) constructs ONE adapter instance per mode from env (UNSILOED_API_KEY present + UNSILOED_MODE=real -> real, else sim) and injects it; nothing in the pipeline imports the adapter concretely — they depend on DenialParserPort only.

capability: Mid-tier reasoning. Two grounded use-cases, both routed to here when PAVO picks the hybrid/mid tier: (1) COMPOSE the agent's next spoken line during a live payer call — a single short, grounded, audit-safe utterance built strictly from retrieved runbook/policy evidence (Moss) + structured call state (denial, claim, IVR position, last payer utterance); (2) INTERPRET an ambiguous free-text denial reason / payer rep utterance into a structured object (canonical denial category, CARC/RARC mapping, the specific contradiction/rebuttal hook to pursue, recommended next dialog act). Output is always grounded in supplied evidence with explicit citations and is forbidden from inventing PHI or clinical facts. This is the reasoning brain between retrieval (Moss) and speech (Qwen TTS / LiveKit transport); PAVO decides whether a turn even reaches MiniMax vs. an on-device line.

real_api.auth_scheme: Bearer token in HTTP header: `Authorization: Bearer ${MINIMAX_API_KEY}`. The MiniMax-native endpoint additionally scopes the account via a GroupId passed as a query parameter (`?GroupId=${MINIMAX_GROUP_ID}`). The OpenAI-compatible endpoint does NOT require GroupId. We target the native endpoint to keep GroupId scoping + native `base_resp` error envelope, and keep the OpenAI-compatible path as a fallback transport. Content-Type: application/json.
real_api.sdk_or_lib: No official Python SDK needed; call REST directly with `httpx.AsyncClient` (async, required because the swarm is asyncio-concurrent — must NOT use the blocking `openai` client in the event loop). MiniMax is OpenAI-API-compatible, so the official `openai` AsyncOpenAI client also works against base_url `https://api.minimax.io/v1` with the OpenAI-compatible route — but we standardize on raw httpx so the adapter owns timeouts, retries, and the native `base_resp` status handling. Pin httpx>=0.27.

endpoints.name: chat completions (native)
endpoints.purpose: Primary call for both compose-line and interpret-denial. Native MiniMax route; returns the `base_resp{status_code,status_msg}` envelope plus OpenAI-shaped `choices`.

request_body.model: MiniMax-M2.1 (configurable via MINIMAX_MODEL; M2.1-highspeed for the latency-sensitive live-call compose path, M3 for harder interpret-denial reasoning)
request_body.messages: [{role: 'system', content: <grounded-NLG contract + guardrails>}, {role: 'user', content: <serialized evidence + call_state + task instruction>}]
request_body.max_completion_tokens: 120 for compose (one spoken line), 400 for interpret (structured JSON)
request_body.response_format: for interpret-denial we request JSON object output and also validate/parse defensively (MiniMax JSON-mode support varies by model; do not rely on it — parse + schema-validate the content string)

endpoints.name: chat completions (OpenAI-compatible fallback)
endpoints.purpose: Drop-in fallback transport if the native route is unavailable; identical OpenAI request/response shape but no `base_resp` envelope and no GroupId query param. Adapter selects route by config flag MINIMAX_ROUTE=native|openai.

real_api.notes: VERIFIED against MiniMax platform docs (platform.minimax.io). Confirmed: base https://api.minimax.io/v1; Bearer-token auth; native chat route is POST /v1/text/chatcompletion_v2 requiring ?GroupId=...; OpenAI-compatible route is POST /v1/chat/completions. Response carries OpenAI-shaped choices[].message.content + usage{prompt_tokens,completion_tokens,total_tokens}; native route adds base_resp{status_code,status_msg} where status_code==0 means success (NON-zero status_code can appear with HTTP 200 — the adapter MUST check base_resp.status_code, not just HTTP status). Model name param uses MiniMax model ids (MiniMax-M2 / M2.1 / M2.5 / M3 and *-highspeed variants); the older `abab*` ids are legacy. UNCERTAIN: exact current default model id and whether GroupId may also be sent as a header on the native route — pin via config (MINIMAX_MODEL, MINIMAX_GROUP_ID) and keep route selectable so a doc drift doesn't require code change. PHI POSTURE (load-bearing): every payload to MiniMax MUST be PHI-redacted FIRST by the TrueFoundry redaction port; MiniMax receives only de-identified tokens (member-id/NPI/name -> stable pseudonyms), and TrueFoundry also meters the call for cost/audit. MiniMax is therefore never a PHI sink.

port_methods.name: compose_line
port_methods.signature: async def compose_line(self, req: ComposeLineRequest) -> ComposeLineResult
port_methods.purpose: Produce ONE grounded spoken line for the agent's next turn, built strictly from req.evidence (retrieved Moss runbook/policy snippets, each with a citation id) + req.call_state (denial summary, claim facts, IVR position, last_payer_utterance, dialog goal). Returns the utterance text, the list of citation ids it relied on, a dialog_act label (e.g. 'state_contradiction','request_reference_number','cite_policy','ask_clarification'), and a grounded:bool / confidence score. MUST refuse (grounded=False + safe fallback line) if evidence is insufficient rather than invent facts.
port_methods.request_shape: ComposeLineRequest{ evidence: list[EvidenceSnippet(id:str, source:str, text:str, score:float)], call_state: CallState(denial_code:str|None, denial_reason:str, claim_facts:dict, ivr_position:str, last_payer_utterance:str|None, dialog_goal:str), max_words:int=40, locale:str='en-US' }
port_methods.result_shape: ComposeLineResult{ line:str, dialog_act:str, citations:list[str], grounded:bool, confidence:float, model:str, tokens:TokenUsage, adapter:str('minimax-real'|'minimax-sim') }

port_methods.name: interpret_denial
port_methods.signature: async def interpret_denial(self, req: InterpretDenialRequest) -> DenialInterpretation
port_methods.purpose: Turn an ambiguous free-text denial reason or live payer-rep utterance into a structured, actionable object: canonical denial category, mapped CARC/RARC code(s), the specific contradiction/rebuttal hook to pursue (grounded in supplied evidence), recommended routing (appeal | resubmit | peer_to_peer | request_records), and the next dialog act. Grounded in req.evidence; flags ambiguity when the text underdetermines the category.
port_methods.result_shape: DenialInterpretation{ category:str, carc_codes:list[str], rarc_codes:list[str], rebuttal_hook:str, recommended_route:str, next_dialog_act:str, citations:list[str], ambiguous:bool, confidence:float, model:str, tokens:TokenUsage, adapter:str }

port_methods.name: health
port_methods.signature: async def health(self) -> PortHealth
port_methods.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe used by the composition root and /health route; real adapter does a cheap auth-scoped ping (or cached short-TTL check), sim adapter returns ready=True with mode='sim'. Returns PortHealth{ready:bool, mode:str, detail:str}.

real_adapter: File: orchestrator/backstop/adapters/minimax_real.py — class MiniMaxReasoningAdapter(ReasoningPort). ONE responsibility: translate ReasoningPort calls into MiniMax REST calls and back. Construction is pure DI: __init__(self, http: httpx.AsyncClient, settings: MiniMaxSettings, prompts: PromptBuilder, clock: Clock). It does NOT create its own client or read os.environ — the composition root injects a shared, connection-pooled httpx.AsyncClient (with timeouts) and a frozen MiniMaxSettings(api_key, group_id, base_url, model, route, compose_max_tokens, interpret_max_tokens, compose_temp, interpret_temp). Flow for compose_line/interpret_denial: (1) PromptBuilder renders the system contract + user payload from request dataclasses into the messages array — system message hard-codes the grounding contract ('use ONLY the numbered evidence; cite ids; never invent member data or clinical facts; if evidence is insufficient, set grounded=false and emit the safe fallback'); (2) POST to the configured route (native /v1/text/chatcompletion_v2?GroupId=... or OpenAI-compat /v1/chat/completions) with model/messages/temperature/max_completion_tokens; (3) check transport: raise MiniMaxTransportError on non-2xx or httpx error; on native route ALSO check base_resp.status_code != 0 -> raise MiniMaxApiError(status_code,status_msg); inspect output_sensitive/content_filter and downgrade to grounded=False fallback if the model refused; (4) parse choices[0].message.content — for compose, the content IS the line (strip, enforce max_words, derive dialog_act from a returned tag or a classifier); for interpret, parse the JSON object content, schema-validate with the DenialInterpretation parser, and on parse failure retry once with a 'return valid JSON only' nudge then fall back to ambiguous=True; (5) map usage -> TokenUsage and stamp adapter='minimax-real', model=resp.model. Resilience: bounded retries (2) with jittered backoff on 429/5xx/timeout via a small retry helper (idempotent because temperature is low and calls are stateless); per-call timeout from settings; all exceptions are typed (MiniMaxTransportError/MiniMaxApiError/MiniMaxParseError) so the Service layer can degrade to the sim adapter or an on-device line. The adapter assumes inbound text is ALREADY PHI-redacted (redaction happens upstream in the Service via the redaction port) and never logs message bodies — only ids, token counts, latency, finish_reason.
sim_adapter: File: orchestrator/backstop/adapters/minimax_sim.py — class MiniMaxSimReasoningAdapter(ReasoningPort). A REAL local grounded-NLG + denial-classification engine, NOT an echo and NOT a network call. Same constructor-injected dependencies minus the http client: __init__(self, lexicon: DenialLexicon, nlg: GroundedNLG, clock: Clock). compose_line works as genuine slot-filling NLG: (1) rank req.evidence by score and lexical overlap with call_state.dialog_goal + last_payer_utterance using a real TF-IDF/cosine scorer (reuse the same TF-IDF utility the Moss sim uses, kept in a shared text util module — single responsibility, no duplication); (2) select the top-1/2 grounded snippets; if the best score is below a threshold, return grounded=False with a deterministic safe fallback line ('I want to make sure I cite the correct policy — can you give me the specific reason code on file?') so insufficient-evidence behavior matches the real adapter's contract; (3) choose a dialog_act by matching call_state against a rule table (e.g. denial mentions 'not medically necessary' + evidence contains an LCD/policy snippet -> 'cite_policy'; payer asks for a number -> 'request_reference_number'); (4) realize the line by filling a vetted, audit-safe template for that dialog_act with the claim facts + the cited snippet's key phrase, then enforce max_words. It composes from evidence + state — different inputs yield genuinely different, grounded lines. interpret_denial uses a real classifier: a curated CARC/RARC lexicon (data/carc_rarc.json: code -> {category, canonical_reason, default_route, rebuttal_template}) plus keyword/regex denial-reason matching over denial_text; it maps to category + codes, picks recommended_route from the lexicon (appeal/resubmit/peer_to_peer/request_records), grounds rebuttal_hook against the best-matching evidence snippet (or marks ambiguous=True when multiple categories tie or no code matches), and sets next_dialog_act consistently. Both methods emit the SAME dataclasses as the real adapter with adapter='minimax-sim', a synthetic-but-real TokenUsage (word counts), confidence from the actual match scores, and citations to real evidence ids. Because the sim is deterministic and offline it doubles as the test double for every Service-layer test and as the runtime fallback when MiniMax is down or PAVO declines the cloud tier.
wiring: Layering Controller -> Service -> Port -> Adapter, wired by the composition root (orchestrator/backstop/composition.py / DI container). (1) Port lives at orchestrator/backstop/ports/reasoning_port.py (abstract ReasoningPort + the request/result dataclasses). (2) Both adapters are bound in the composition root: it reads settings, decides real vs sim from MINIMAX_MODE (real|sim) and/or PAVO's per-turn tier decision, constructs the shared httpx.AsyncClient + MiniMaxSettings for the real adapter and the DenialLexicon/GroundedNLG for the sim, and provides a ReasoningPort to the Service. (3) Invocation point in the pipeline: in call.py's per-turn PAVO loop (the PAVO step). Sequence per agent turn: PAVO router scores the turn -> if it routes to the cloud/hybrid (mid-tier reasoning) tier, the TurnService (a) calls Moss RetrievalPort to fetch evidence, (b) passes evidence+state through the TrueFoundry RedactionPort so only de-identified text leaves the boundary, (c) calls ReasoningPort.compose_line (or interpret_denial when the last payer utterance is an ambiguous denial reason) to get the grounded line + dialog_act + citations, (d) hands the line to the Qwen TTS port and LiveKit transport port for speech, while citations + dialog_act + token usage flow into the per-appeal evidence timeline and the TrueFoundry audit/cost ledger. If PAVO routes to ondevice_fast, or the real adapter raises/refuses, the Service uses the sim ReasoningPort as the degraded path — identical interface, so call.py is unchanged. The grounded line + citations later feed letter.py so the verbatim appeal letter is traceable to the same evidence the agent spoke. swarm.py runs many such TurnServices concurrently; concurrency is bounded by the AWS burst port (Semaphore in sim), and each MiniMax call is an awaited async REST call on the shared client, so the swarm is not serialized.

tests.description: Port-level contract suite, parametrized over BOTH adapters (real adapter driven against a mocked httpx transport via httpx.MockTransport; sim adapter run for real). Asserts every adapter honors the ReasoningPort contract identically: compose_line returns a ComposeLineResult whose line is <= max_words; citations is a subset of the supplied evidence ids (NEVER cites an id that was not provided = no fabrication); grounded=False yields the deterministic safe fallback and empty/limited citations; dialog_act is in the allowed enum; interpret_denial returns category/codes/route in their allowed enums and citations subset evidence ids; adapter field is correct. Same test body, two fixtures — proves substitutability.

Real adapter against httpx.MockTransport (no network). Cases: (a) native happy path -> request goes to /v1/text/chatcompletion_v2 with ?GroupId=, Authorization: Bearer header set, model/temperature/max_completion_tokens from settings; response choices[0].message.content parsed into line; usage mapped to TokenUsage. (b) base_resp.status_code != 0 with HTTP 200 -> raises MiniMaxApiError (proves we don't trust HTTP status alone). (c) 429 then 200 -> retry succeeds; 3x 5xx -> MiniMaxTransportError after bounded retries. (d) output_sensitive/content_filter finish_reason -> downgrades to grounded=False fallback. (e) interpret_denial with malformed JSON content -> one retry nudge, then ambiguous=True fallback (MiniMaxParseError path). (f) OpenAI-compatible route flag -> hits /v1/chat/completions with no GroupId and no base_resp check. (g) asserts NO PHI is logged and message bodies are never emitted to the logger (capture logs).

Sim adapter as a REAL engine. Cases: (a) given two different evidence sets + call states, compose_line returns two DIFFERENT grounded lines that each cite the actually-best evidence id (proves it's NLG, not echo, and is grounded). (b) when all evidence scores below threshold -> grounded=False + exact safe fallback line. (c) dialog_act rule table: 'not medically necessary' + LCD snippet -> 'cite_policy'; payer asks for a number -> 'request_reference_number'. (d) interpret_denial: CARC 50 ('not deemed a medical necessity') text -> category='medical_necessity', recommended_route in {'appeal','peer_to_peer'}, rebuttal_hook grounded in evidence; CARC 16 ('missing/incomplete info') -> route='resubmit'. (e) ambiguous text with no code match / tie -> ambiguous=True. (f) determinism: identical input twice -> identical output (so it's a stable test double).

Service/use-case wiring with the sim adapter injected as the ReasoningPort test double and fakes for Moss/Redaction/TTS ports. Asserts: (a) on a hybrid/cloud-tier turn the Service calls RedactionPort BEFORE ReasoningPort (no raw PHI string ever reaches the reasoning adapter — assert the adapter received only redacted tokens). (b) the composed line + citations are forwarded to the evidence timeline and to the TTS port. (c) when the (mocked real) ReasoningPort raises MiniMaxTransportError, the Service falls back to the sim ReasoningPort and the turn still completes (degraded path). (d) when PAVO routes ondevice_fast, ReasoningPort.compose_line is NOT called at all.

capability: Brand-voice multilingual TTS. Synthesizes the agent's spoken appeals-coordinator line — the exact words MiniMax composed for a turn — into playable audio using ONE cloned/branded coordinator voice (Qwen3-TTS / CosyVoice). Multilingual (member may need ES/ZH); audio is the payload pushed over LiveKit transport to the (sandbox) IVR and is what the nurse hears on barge-in. Sim adapter must produce a VALID playable 16-bit PCM WAV with real samples (a synthesized formant/tone envelope of the right duration), never a 24-byte fake or an echo.
keys_needed: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY (canonical DashScope key; either env var resolves to the same Bearer token)
QWEN_TTS_MODEL (optional; default 'qwen3-tts-flash' for built-in voices, 'cosyvoice-v3.5-plus' when a cloned voice_id is configured)
QWEN_VOICE_ID (optional; the cloned coordinator voice_id from enrollment, e.g. 'cosyvoice-v3.5-plus-coordinator-xxxxxxxx'; falls back to built-in 'Cherry' if unset)
QWEN_MODE (real | sim; per-adapter mode flag, mirrors other integrations)

real_api.base_url: https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com (Singapore/intl) or https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com (Beijing/cn). Region-selected by QWEN_REGION.
real_api.auth_scheme: HTTP Bearer token in the Authorization header: 'Authorization: Bearer ${DASHSCOPE_API_KEY}'. Content-Type: application/json. Optional 'X-DashScope-DataInspection: enable'. port_name: SpeechSynthesisPort (a.k.a. TtsPort) — the brand-voice TTS capability. One responsibility: text -> playable audio bytes in the coordinator voice. Lives at orchestrator/backstop/ports/speech_synthesis_port.py.

port_methods.signature: async def synth(self, req: SynthRequest) -> SynthResult
port_methods.purpose: Whole-line synthesis. Takes a SynthRequest(text: str, voice_id: Optional[str]=None, language: Language=Language.EN, sample_rate: int=24000) and returns SynthResult(audio: bytes  # complete WAV container, real PCM samples, sample_rate: int, channels: int, sample_width_bytes: int, duration_ms: int, voice_id: str, mode: Literal['real','sim'], cost_chars: int). The returned bytes MUST be a valid, playable WAV (RIFF/WAVE header + PCM data) for BOTH adapters. Used to render a full composed spoken line for one turn.

port_methods.signature: async def synth_stream(self, req: SynthRequest) -> AsyncIterator[AudioFrame]
port_methods.purpose: Low-latency streaming synthesis. Yields AudioFrame(pcm: bytes, sample_rate: int, channels: int, seq: int) raw-PCM frames as they are produced, for piping into LiveKit with minimal first-audio latency and to support nurse barge-in (cancellation mid-stream). Real adapter uses the WS realtime endpoint; sim adapter chunks its locally-generated PCM into frames. Default port impl MAY derive synth_stream by chunking synth()'s output so simple adapters only implement synth().

port_methods.purpose: Typed boundary objects so Controller/Service never see vendor JSON. SynthRequest.text is asserted PHI-redacted by the Service before it reaches the port (the port contract documents this precondition).

real_adapter: orchestrator/backstop/integrations/qwen.py :: QwenTtsAdapter(SpeechSynthesisPort). One responsibility: translate SynthRequest <-> DashScope HTTP/WS and return WAV bytes. Construction (DI): QwenTtsAdapter(http: httpx.AsyncClient, api_key: str, region: str='intl', model: str='qwen3-tts-flash', default_voice_id: str='Cherry', clock=time.monotonic) — all collaborators injected; no module-level globals, no SDK singleton. synth(): POST {model, input:{text, voice: req.voice_id or default_voice_id, language_type: map(req.language)}} to /api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation with Bearer header; parse output.audio.url; GET the url bytes (same injected client, bounded timeout); validate the bytes parse as a RIFF/WAVE PCM stream via stdlib wave (reject empty/HTML/expired-URL bodies); normalize to req.sample_rate if needed; return SynthResult(audio=wav_bytes, mode='real', cost_chars=len(text), duration_ms=computed_from_frames, voice_id=resolved). If the response carries inline base64 (voice-design/preview path), base64-decode and wrap with wave instead of fetching a URL. synth_stream(): open WSS to /api-ws/v1/realtime, send session.update {voice, response_format:'PCM_24000HZ_MONO_16BIT', mode:'server_commit'}, append text + commit, base64-decode each response.audio.delta into AudioFrame(seq++) until response.done; on cancellation (nurse barge-in) close the socket promptly. health(): query_voice for the configured cloned voice_id (skip if a built-in voice), cache result for N seconds. Errors map to typed SynthError (auth, rate-limit/429 with Retry-After, expired-url, malformed-audio, timeout) — never leak raw httpx/vendor exceptions across the port. Cost (cost_chars) is reported to the TrueFoundry cost meter by the Service, not by this adapter (single responsibility). No ret/PHI logging: text is never logged.
sim_adapter: orchestrator/backstop/integrations/qwen_sim.py :: SimTtsAdapter(SpeechSynthesisPort). REAL local DSP — NOT an echo, NOT a 24-byte stub. Produces a genuine, playable mono 16-bit PCM WAV whose DURATION is derived from the input text and whose WAVEFORM is a deterministic synthesized speech-like envelope, so downstream code (WAV decode, LiveKit framing, duration math, nurse playback, tests) all behave exactly as with the real adapter. Algorithm (pure stdlib: math, struct, wave, io, hashlib, base64): (1) Estimate duration = max(MIN_MS, words * MS_PER_WORD) using a configurable speaking rate (~165 wpm default) plus per-sentence pauses, so a longer appeal line yields a longer WAV — this is the genuine 'work'. (2) Build a per-character pseudo-formant generator: hash(voice_id + text) seeds a deterministic RNG so the SAME request always yields byte-identical audio (testability); for each phoneme-slot derive a fundamental f0 (voice_id sets the base pitch band so different voices sound different) plus 2-3 formant partials, apply a short ADSR amplitude envelope per syllable and inter-word silences, summing sine partials sample-by-sample at the requested sample_rate (default 24000). (3) Clamp to int16, write a proper RIFF/WAVE header via the wave module (nchannels=1, sampwidth=2, framerate=sample_rate), return SynthResult(audio=wav_bytes, mode='sim', cost_chars=len(text), duration_ms=actual, voice_id=req.voice_id or 'sim-coordinator'). synth_stream() slices that PCM into fixed-size AudioFrames (e.g. 20ms) and yields them with a tiny await sleep to emulate streaming/barge-in. health() -> PortHealth(ok=True, mode='sim'). The output is intentionally intelligible-shaped (varying pitch/amplitude that tracks the text) rather than flat noise, so a human listening to the dashboard hears a plausible voice-like tone of the correct length — demonstrating the pipeline end-to-end with zero external calls and zero PHI egress. Deterministic => unit-testable byte-for-byte.
wiring: Layering: Controller -> Service -> SpeechSynthesisPort -> {QwenTtsAdapter | SimTtsAdapter}, wired in the composition root. (1) COMPOSITION ROOT (orchestrator/backstop/composition.py / DI container): reads QWEN_MODE (or auto: real if DASHSCOPE_API_KEY/QWEN_API_KEY present AND health() ok, else sim) and binds SpeechSynthesisPort to QwenTtsAdapter(real) or SimTtsAdapter. The chosen adapter is injected into the VoiceTurnService — neither the Service nor call.py imports qwen.py directly. (2) HOT PATH (per-turn PAVO loop, call.py): the turn pipeline is PAVO-router decides action -> Moss retrieves rebuttal -> MiniMax composes the spoken line (mid-tier reasoning) -> TrueFoundry redaction port asserts/strips PHI from that line -> SpeechSynthesisPort.synth()/synth_stream() renders coordinator-voice audio -> LiveKit transport adapter pushes the audio frames onto the call (sandbox IVR) and to the nurse monitor channel. Qwen sits squarely between 'compose line' and 'play line', invoked once per agent utterance. PHI PRECONDITION: the Service guarantees req.text passed to synth() has already gone through the TrueFoundry redact port — a guard in VoiceTurnService raises if an un-redacted marker is detected, so PHI never reaches Qwen (third-party, no BAA). (3) BARGE-IN: synth_stream() supports cancellation so a nurse barge-in over LiveKit stops synthesis immediately. (4) COST/AUDIT: VoiceTurnService reports SynthResult.cost_chars + voice_id + mode to the TrueFoundry cost/audit ports (keeps qwen.py single-responsibility). (5) FEATURE SUBSTRATE: the same port renders the read-aloud of the final appeal letter summary in the nurse review queue, and multilingual member-facing lines — both call SpeechSynthesisPort, swappable real/sim.

capability: Real-time voice transport for the agent swarm: each concurrent payer call runs over a LiveKit room, and a human appeals nurse can be bridged into any live call (barge-in / takeover) by minting a short-lived, scoped access token. The port mints signed access tokens (room-scoped JWT grants), manages room lifecycle (create/delete/list), enumerates live participants, and forcibly removes a participant. PAVO-driven audio frames and the nurse's barge-in audio flow over the same room transport.

real_api.base_url: Two surfaces. (1) Token minting is OFFLINE/local crypto — no network call: an HS256 JWT is signed with LIVEKIT_API_SECRET. (2) Server RoomService is HTTP via Twirp at the LIVEKIT_URL host. LIVEKIT_URL is typically a wss:// signaling URL (e.g. wss://backstop-xyz.livekit.cloud); the RoomService HTTP base is the same host over https (https://backstop-xyz.livekit.cloud). Twirp endpoints live under POST /twirp/livekit.RoomService/<MethodName>.
real_api.auth_scheme: Bearer JWT (HS256). The JWT is signed with LIVEKIT_API_SECRET; claim iss = LIVEKIT_API_KEY, sub = participant identity, exp/nbf set TTL (SDK DEFAULT_TTL = 6h), and a custom 'video' grant claim object scopes permissions. Participant-join tokens carry video.roomJoin=true + video.room=<roomName> (+ canPublish/canSubscribe/canPublishData). RoomService management calls require a token whose grants include roomCreate (CreateRoom/DeleteRoom), roomList (ListRooms), or roomAdmin (ListParticipants/RemoveParticipant). The token goes in HTTP header 'Authorization: Bearer <jwt>'.

endpoints.name: Mint access token (local, no HTTP)
endpoints.produces: a compact HS256 JWT string. Claims: {iss: API_KEY, sub: identity, nbf, exp, video: {room, roomJoin, canPublish, canSubscribe, canPublishData, hidden, roomAdmin?, roomCreate?}}
endpoints.notes: Pure crypto via PyJWT under the hood: jwt.encode(claims, api_secret, algorithm='HS256'). Verified with api.TokenVerifier(api_key, api_secret).verify(token).

endpoints.name: CreateRoom
endpoints.response: Room {sid, name, empty_timeout, max_participants, creation_time, metadata, num_participants, active_recording}

endpoints.name: ListParticipants
endpoints.response: ListParticipantsResponse {participants: list<ParticipantInfo{sid, identity, name, state, tracks, metadata, joined_at, is_publisher}>}

real_api.sdk_or_lib: livekit-api (pip install livekit-api) — provides livekit.api.AccessToken, VideoGrants, TokenVerifier, LiveKitAPI, RoomServiceClient, and the *Request dataclasses. Async client uses aiohttp; remember await lkapi.aclose(). Token signing uses PyJWT (HS256). Optional: livekit (livekit-rtc) for an in-process audio participant, only needed if we publish/subscribe real audio frames; not required for token+room lifecycle.
real_api.notes: CONFIRMED from LiveKit source (livekit-api access_token.py): DEFAULT_TTL = timedelta(hours=6); to_jwt() does jwt.encode(claims, api_secret, algorithm='HS256'); AccessToken reads LIVEKIT_API_KEY/LIVEKIT_API_SECRET from env when args omitted; VideoGrants snake_case fields include room_create, room_list, room_record, room_admin, room_join, room, can_publish, can_subscribe, can_publish_data, hidden, recorder. RoomService is Twirp (POST + protobuf/JSON) under /twirp/livekit.RoomService/. UNCERTAIN: LIVEKIT_URL scheme handling — LiveKit Cloud gives a wss:// URL; LiveKitAPI accepts the https/wss host and normalizes internally, but for self-host confirm the http(s) RoomService port (default 7880). For Backstop we keep TTL short (e.g. 15 min for call tokens, 5 min for nurse barge-in tokens) rather than the 6h default, to bound PHI/transport exposure.

port_methods.name: open_channel
port_methods.signature: async def open_channel(self, call_id: str, *, max_participants: int = 4, ttl: timedelta = timedelta(minutes=15), metadata: str | None = None) -> Channel
port_methods.purpose: Provision a transport channel (LiveKit room) for one payer call and return a Channel handle {channel_id, room_name, agent_token, expires_at}. Idempotent on call_id (room name = f'appeal-{call_id}'). The returned agent_token is a join-scoped JWT for the swarm's voice agent (canPublish/canSubscribe/canPublishData, NOT admin).

port_methods.name: mint_join_token
port_methods.signature: def mint_join_token(self, *, channel_id: str, identity: str, display_name: str, can_publish: bool = True, can_subscribe: bool = True, ttl: timedelta = timedelta(minutes=15), admin: bool = False) -> JoinToken
port_methods.purpose: Mint a signed, room-scoped access token (JoinToken{token, identity, room, expires_at}) for a specific participant. Pure-crypto, no I/O. Used for the voice agent and (with a fresh short TTL) for the nurse bridging in.

port_methods.name: bridge_nurse
port_methods.signature: async def bridge_nurse(self, *, channel_id: str, nurse_id: str, can_publish: bool = True, ttl: timedelta = timedelta(minutes=5)) -> JoinToken
port_methods.purpose: Barge-in: produce a short-lived nurse JoinToken scoped to the live call's channel so the human can listen/talk on the existing call. Validates the channel is live first (raises ChannelNotFound otherwise). This is the load-bearing 'hand a human into the call' capability.

port_methods.name: list_participants
port_methods.signature: async def list_participants(self, channel_id: str) -> list[Participant]
port_methods.purpose: Enumerate who is currently on the call (agent, nurse, simulated payer rep) as Participant{identity, name, is_publisher, joined_at}. Powers the per-appeal evidence timeline / live call roster in the dashboard.

port_methods.name: remove_participant
port_methods.signature: async def remove_participant(self, *, channel_id: str, identity: str) -> None
port_methods.purpose: Forcibly eject a participant (e.g. kill a runaway agent, or end the nurse's session). Maps to RemoveParticipant; admin-scoped.

port_methods.name: close_channel
port_methods.signature: async def close_channel(self, channel_id: str) -> None
port_methods.purpose: Tear down the channel when the call ends/aborts (maps to DeleteRoom). Critical for cleanup — fixes the 'fire-and-forget / never cleaned' class of resource leaks for transport.

port_methods.name: verify_token
port_methods.signature: def verify_token(self, token: str) -> Claims
port_methods.purpose: Decode + signature-verify a token, returning Claims{identity, room, grants, expires_at}. Used by the WS/HTTP edge to authorize an incoming participant or nurse-bridge request without trusting client-supplied identity. Sim and real must agree on the claim shape (contract-tested).

real_adapter: LiveKitVoiceTransportAdapter implements VoiceTransportPort using the livekit-api SDK. Construction takes (url, api_key, api_secret) injected from config (no env reads inside the adapter — composition root resolves them). One file, one responsibility: translate VoiceTransportPort calls into LiveKit primitives. open_channel(): builds room_name = f'appeal-{call_id}', calls await lkapi.room.create_room(api.CreateRoomRequest(name=room_name, empty_timeout=300, max_participants=max_participants, metadata=metadata)), then mints an agent join token and returns Channel. mint_join_token()/bridge_nurse(): build api.AccessToken(api_key, api_secret).with_identity(identity).with_name(display_name).with_ttl(ttl).with_grants(api.VideoGrants(room_join=True, room=room_name, can_publish=can_publish, can_subscribe=can_subscribe, can_publish_data=True, room_admin=admin)).to_jwt(); bridge_nurse first calls list_participants to assert the room is live. list_participants(): await lkapi.room.list_participants(api.ListParticipantsRequest(room=room_name)) mapped to Participant DTOs. remove_participant(): await lkapi.room.remove_participant(api.RemoveParticipantRequest(room=room_name, identity=identity)). close_channel(): await lkapi.room.delete_room(api.DeleteRoomRequest(room=room_name)) (swallow not-found as idempotent). verify_token(): api.TokenVerifier(api_key, api_secret).verify(token) → Claims. Holds a single LiveKitAPI(url, api_key, api_secret) instance; exposes async aclose() that calls lkapi.aclose() for graceful shutdown. Maps LiveKit/Twirp errors to domain errors (ChannelNotFound, TransportError) so the Service layer never sees vendor types. TTLs deliberately short (15 min agent / 5 min nurse) to bound PHI exposure on the wire.
sim_adapter: InProcessVoiceTransportAdapter implements VoiceTransportPort as a REAL local transport — not an echo. It maintains an in-memory registry of channels {channel_id -> _SimRoom{room_name, participants: dict[identity -> Participant], created_at, max_participants}} guarded by an asyncio.Lock, plus an in-process asyncio pub/sub fabric so audio/data frames published by one participant are actually delivered to the others (each participant gets an asyncio.Queue; publish fans out to all other subscribers' queues — genuine concurrent transport that the call.py PAVO loop and a barge-in nurse can both attach to). Crucially, its tokens are REAL HS256 JWTs: it signs with a configured dev secret using PyJWT (jwt.encode(claims, secret, algorithm='HS256')) and verify_token() does jwt.decode(...) — so claim shape, signature, exp/nbf, and the 'video' grant block are byte-compatible with the real adapter and pass the same contract tests. open_channel creates a _SimRoom and enforces max_participants; bridge_nurse mints a short-TTL nurse token and registers a nurse participant on the live room (raises ChannelNotFound if the room was never opened or was closed) and wires its queue into the fabric so the nurse hears the live call; list_participants returns the live roster; remove_participant drops the participant and closes its queue (delivering a 'left' event); close_channel deletes the room and drains all queues. This lets the entire swarm run end-to-end with zero network and zero LiveKit account, while exercising real concurrency, real token crypto, real join/barge-in/eject semantics, and real frame delivery.
wiring: Layering: Controller -> Service -> VoiceTransportPort -> {LiveKit|InProcess} Adapter, wired by the composition root / DI container. (1) Composition root (e.g. orchestrator/backstop/composition.py) reads LIVEKIT_URL/API_KEY/API_SECRET via the config object and binds VoiceTransportPort to LiveKitVoiceTransportAdapter when livekit.mode == 'real', else InProcessVoiceTransportAdapter; the chosen mode is surfaced in the integrations status panel. (2) SwarmService (swarm.py use-case) — when a denial detonates and the orchestrator spawns N concurrent calls, it calls await transport.open_channel(call_id, ...) per call to provision the room and obtain the agent join token; the AWS burst-concurrency port/semaphore caps how many channels are opened at once. (3) CallService (call.py per-turn PAVO loop) — the agent participant joins the channel with its token; each turn, PAVO-routed audio (composed by MiniMax, voiced by Qwen TTS) is published over the channel, and inbound IVR/payer audio is subscribed from it; channel_id is recorded on the appeal's evidence timeline. (4) Nurse barge-in path: the nurse review-queue Controller (server.py route, AUTHENTICATED — fixes the no-auth vuln) calls NurseBridgeService.bridge_into(call_id, nurse_id) -> await transport.bridge_nurse(channel_id, nurse_id, ttl=5min); the returned short-lived JoinToken is handed to the dashboard for the nurse client to connect — supporting the live takeover before the cryptographic sign-off gate. (5) WS/HTTP edge calls transport.verify_token(...) to authorize incoming participants instead of trusting client identity (closes the unauthenticated-WS / no-origin-check gaps for the voice surface). (6) Lifecycle: on call completion/abort and on graceful shutdown, the Service calls await transport.close_channel(channel_id) and the adapter's aclose() — fixing fire-and-forget tasks / no-graceful-shutdown / never-cleaned-resources for transport. Tokens are never logged; only claim metadata (identity, room, exp) goes to the TrueFoundry audit port.

tests.name: test_port_contract_run_against_both_adapters
tests.asserts: Both adapters satisfy the VoiceTransportPort contract identically. Single parametrized suite (pytest fixture yields each adapter): open_channel returns a Channel with non-empty room_name + agent_token + future expires_at; mint_join_token returns a non-empty token; list_participants on a fresh channel is empty; bridge_nurse on an unknown channel raises ChannelNotFound; close_channel is idempotent. The LiveKit instance uses a mocked LiveKitAPI/room client (no network) so the contract — not the wire — is under test.

tests.name: test_minted_token_is_valid_hs256_with_video_grant
tests.asserts: Token minted by mint_join_token(channel_id, identity='agent-7', room scoped) decodes under jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=['HS256']) and contains iss=api_key, sub='agent-7', exp>nbf, and claims['video'] with room==room_name, roomJoin==True, canPublish/canSubscribe/canPublishData set. verify_token(token) returns Claims with matching identity+room. A tampered token (flip one char of signature) makes verify_token raise. Proves sim does REAL crypto, not an echo, and is byte-compatible with real.
