tests.asserts: mint_join_token(admin=False) produces a grant WITHOUT roomAdmin/roomCreate; admin=True (management token) includes roomAdmin. Verifies the least-privilege scoping that lets the WS edge reject participant tokens attempting admin actions.

tests.name: test_inprocess_real_frame_delivery_between_participants
tests.asserts: Open a channel, register agent + nurse, agent publishes a data/audio frame; nurse's subscription queue actually receives that exact frame and agent does not receive its own. Proves the sim is a genuine in-process transport (fan-out pub/sub), not a string echo — the core mandate.

tests.name: test_bridge_nurse_into_live_call
tests.asserts: After open_channel + agent join, bridge_nurse adds the nurse to the SAME room: list_participants now includes both identities; nurse token is room-scoped to that room; nurse can publish and the agent receives it (barge-in works). bridge_nurse on a closed channel raises ChannelNotFound.

tests.name: test_max_participants_enforced
tests.asserts: open_channel(max_participants=2); adding a 3rd participant raises ChannelFull. Mirrors LiveKit room max_participants so the sim has real backpressure semantics.

tests.name: test_remove_and_close_cleanup
tests.asserts: remove_participant drops the identity from list_participants and closes its queue (sim); close_channel removes the channel so subsequent list_participants/bridge_nurse raise ChannelNotFound; close_channel twice does not raise (idempotent). Validates the leak-fix lifecycle.

tests.name: test_real_adapter_calls_correct_sdk_with_expected_payloads
tests.asserts: With LiveKitAPI/room mocked: open_channel calls room.create_room with CreateRoomRequest(name='appeal-<id>', max_participants, metadata); close_channel calls room.delete_room(DeleteRoomRequest(room='appeal-<id>')); list_participants calls room.list_participants(ListParticipantsRequest(room=...)) and maps ParticipantInfo->Participant; remove_participant calls room.remove_participant(...). Confirms the Twirp method/argument contract without a live server.

tests.name: test_real_adapter_maps_vendor_errors_to_domain_errors
tests.asserts: When the mocked room client raises a Twirp not-found on delete/list, the adapter raises domain ChannelNotFound (not the vendor exception); generic failures map to TransportError. Keeps vendor types out of the Service layer (hexagonal boundary).

tests.name: test_swarm_service_provisions_and_tears_down_channel
tests.asserts: Detonating a denial opens one channel per spawned call (bounded by the concurrency-cap port), the call publishes/subscribes turns over it, and on completion/abort close_channel is invoked exactly once per channel (assert via spy). Proves the wiring + lifecycle end-to-end with zero network.

tests.name: test_aclose_graceful_shutdown
tests.asserts: adapter.aclose() awaits lkapi.aclose() exactly once; safe to call when no channels open. Backs the graceful-shutdown vuln fix.

capability: Elastic burst compute that gates swarm concurrency. The swarm fans out N parallel voice-agent appeals against payer lines; AWS provides an admission-control "slot" before each appeal-worker starts so the system can scale to hundreds of concurrent workers under load and idle to zero between batches. The port hides whether a slot is backed by a real AWS Fargate task in a managed pool (real adapter) or by an in-process asyncio.Semaphore (sim adapter). It is pure backpressure/capacity management — it does NOT touch PHI, payer data, or call content; it only meters concurrency.
keys_needed: BACKSTOP_ECS_CLUSTER (cluster name/ARN hosting the worker pool)
BACKSTOP_ECS_TASK_DEFINITION (family:revision of the appeal-worker task def)
BACKSTOP_ECS_CONTAINER_NAME (container name inside the task def, for overrides)
BACKSTOP_MAX_CONCURRENCY (hard ceiling on simultaneous slots; default 200)
BACKSTOP_ECS_ASSIGN_PUBLIC_IP (ENABLED|DISABLED; default DISABLED for private subnets+NAT)
BACKSTOP_ECS_CAPACITY_PROVIDER (FARGATE|FARGATE_SPOT; default FARGATE for steady, FARGATE_SPOT for cheap burst)

real_api.base_url: https://ecs.<AWS_REGION>.amazonaws.com (AWS ECS regional endpoint; accessed via boto3/aioboto3, not raw HTTP). The sister Service Quotas endpoint https://servicequotas.<AWS_REGION>.amazonaws.com is used read-only to discover the account's Fargate vCPU ceiling.
real_api.auth_scheme: AWS SigV4 request signing using AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (+ optional AWS_SESSION_TOKEN for assumed roles). boto3/botocore performs the signing automatically from the standard credential chain (env vars > shared config > instance/role). IAM principal must be granted ecs:RunTask, ecs:StopTask, ecs:DescribeTasks, ecs:ListTasks on the cluster + task definition, plus iam:PassRole for the task's executionRoleArn/taskRoleArn, and (read-only) servicequotas:GetServiceQuota.

endpoints.purpose: Launch a Fargate task = acquire a compute slot. Called when the pool needs to grow to admit a queued appeal-worker.

request.count: 1 (one task per slot; max 10 per call so batches of >10 loop)
request.capacityProviderStrategy: [{capacityProvider: FARGATE|FARGATE_SPOT, weight: 1, base: 0}]  (mutually exclusive with launchType; preferred so FARGATE_SPOT burst is possible)
request.startedBy: backstop-swarm (<=128 chars, used for ListTasks filtering)
request.clientToken: <uuid> (idempotency: retried RunTask with same token will not double-launch)
request.tags: [{key: app, value: backstop}, {key: pool, value: appeal-worker}]

response.tasks: [{taskArn, taskDefinitionArn, clusterArn, lastStatus(PROVISIONING|PENDING), desiredStatus(RUNNING), containers:[{name,lastStatus,...}], createdAt}]

real_api.sdk_or_lib: boto3 / botocore for sync, aioboto3 (or asyncio loop.run_in_executor wrapping boto3) for the async swarm. Region from AWS_REGION; creds from the default botocore chain. real_api.notes: DESIGN NOTE / honesty: AWS's load-bearing role here is CONCURRENCY ADMISSION, not running each appeal inside Fargate. The appeal logic (PAVO loop, Moss retrieval, etc.) runs in the orchestrator process; the Fargate task pool is the *capacity budget* that authorizes how many of those loops may run at once. So the real adapter's acquire() => RunTask+poll-to-RUNNING, release() => StopTask. CONFIDENCE: the ecs run_task/describe_tasks/stop_task/list_tasks request+response shapes, the FARGATE_SPOT capacityProviderStrategy constraint (mutually exclusive with launchType), the 'RESOURCE:FARGATE' quota-exhaustion failure reason, and SigV4/IAM actions are all confirmed against current boto3 docs. LESS CERTAIN, flagged: the exact Service Quotas QuotaCode L-3032A538 / ServiceCode 'fargate' string can drift by account/region — the real adapter must treat a quota-lookup miss as non-fatal and fall back to BACKSTOP_MAX_CONCURRENCY. Eventual consistency: a freshly-launched taskArn can briefly 404 in describe_tasks; poll with exponential backoff (2s→max ~30s) before treating as failure. Cost/latency caveat: cold RunTask->RUNNING is ~10-60s, too slow to gate per-appeal on the hot path; production should keep a WARM pool (pre-launched idle tasks) and have acquire() check out a warm slot first, only calling RunTask to grow the pool — this is captured in the port via a separate ensure_capacity()/prewarm method so the per-appeal acquire() stays fast.

port_methods.signature: async def acquire(self, *, slot_key: str, timeout: float | None = None) -> Slot
port_methods.purpose: Block until a compute slot is available, then return an opened Slot handle. slot_key is a NON-PHI surrogate (e.g. appeal_id) used only for tracing/idempotency. Raises CapacityTimeout if timeout elapses before a slot frees. This is the call the swarm awaits before starting each appeal worker.

port_methods.signature: async def release(self, slot: Slot) -> None
port_methods.purpose: Return a previously acquired slot to the pool (idempotent: releasing twice is a no-op). Real adapter StopTasks the backing Fargate task or returns it to the warm pool; sim adapter releases the semaphore. Always called in a finally/contextmanager so slots cannot leak on exception.

port_methods.signature: async def __aenter__/__aexit__ via 'async with gate.slot(slot_key) as slot:'  -> AsyncContextManager[Slot]
port_methods.purpose: Ergonomic acquire+guaranteed-release wrapper (default-implemented on the port ABC in terms of acquire/release) so callers can't forget to release on the error path.

port_methods.signature: async def ensure_capacity(self, *, target: int) -> int
port_methods.purpose: Pre-warm / scale the pool toward `target` ready slots (real: RunTask to grow warm pool up to min(target, max_concurrency, quota); sim: no-op returning min(target,max)). Returns the number of slots now provisionable. Lets the swarm pre-scale before a known batch instead of paying cold-start per appeal.

port_methods.signature: async def capacity(self) -> CapacitySnapshot
port_methods.purpose: Return live gauge: CapacitySnapshot(max:int, in_use:int, available:int, warm:int, mode:'real'|'sim'). Powers the dashboard concurrency meter, the cost.py burn estimate, and backpressure decisions in the triage worklist.

port_methods.signature: async def reconcile(self) -> int
port_methods.purpose: Recover true in-use count from the backend after an orchestrator restart (real: ListTasks startedBy=backstop-swarm; sim: returns current semaphore deficit). Returns reconciled in_use. Prevents leaked/double-counted slots across the no-graceful-shutdown vuln fix.

port_methods.signature: async def aclose(self) -> None
port_methods.purpose: Graceful shutdown: stop accepting new acquires, StopTask all warm/idle slots (real) or drain the semaphore (sim). Wired into the FastAPI lifespan shutdown to fix the 'no graceful shutdown' vuln.

real_adapter:
File: orchestrator/backstop/adapters/aws/fargate_gate.py — class FargateConcurrencyGate(ConcurrencyGatePort). ONE responsibility: translate slot acquire/release into Fargate task pool operations. Construction (by the composition root only): takes an injected async ECS client (aioboto3 session client, or a boto3 client wrapped to run in a thread executor), the cluster/taskdef/subnets/sgs/container-name config, max_concurrency, capacity_provider, and a Clock + backoff policy (injected for testability). Holds an internal model: a set of warm (idle, RUNNING) taskArns and a set of in_use taskArns, guarded by an asyncio.Lock with SHORT critical sections (only mutating the sets — never holding the lock across an await on AWS, which fixes the 'lock-scope serializes the swarm' vuln). 

acquire(): (1) fast path — pop a warm taskArn under the lock and move it to in_use; return Slot(task_arn, slot_key). (2) slow path — if no warm slot and in_use < min(max_concurrency, discovered_quota): call ecs.run_task(count=1, capacityProviderStrategy=[{provider, weight:1, base:0}], networkConfiguration, overrides with BACKSTOP_SLOT_ID/APPEAL_ID env, clientToken=uuid for idempotency, startedBy='backstop-swarm'); then poll ecs.describe_tasks with exponential backoff (injected backoff, 2s→~30s cap) until lastStatus==RUNNING; on success register taskArn as in_use and return Slot. (3) if at ceiling or run_task returns failures[].reason startswith 'RESOURCE:FARGATE' (quota exhausted), await on an asyncio.Condition that release() notifies — i.e. block for a freed slot until timeout, then raise CapacityTimeout. 

release(slot): under lock remove from in_use; policy = keep up to a small warm pool (configurable warm_keep), else ecs.stop_task(task=slot.task_arn, reason='backstop: appeal complete'); notify the Condition so a waiting acquire() proceeds. Idempotent via a released-set guard. 

ensure_capacity(target): RunTask in batches of up to 10 (count param max) until warm+in_use == min(target, max, quota); cache the quota from servicequotas.get_service_quota(ServiceCode='fargate', QuotaCode='L-3032A538') on first call, treating any error as 'use max_concurrency'. 

capacity(): snapshot the sets. reconcile(): ecs.list_tasks(startedBy='backstop-swarm', desiredStatus='RUNNING') paginated, then describe_tasks to classify warm vs in_use, rebuilding internal sets. aclose(): set a closed flag, stop_task all warm+in_use. 

All boto exceptions are caught and remapped to domain errors (CapacityTimeout, CapacityBackendError) so the Service layer never sees botocore types — keeps the port abstraction clean. No PHI ever enters env overrides or tags (only the surrogate appeal_id and slot uuid).
sim_adapter:
File: orchestrator/backstop/adapters/aws/semaphore_gate.py — class SemaphoreConcurrencyGate(ConcurrencyGatePort). This is REAL local backpressure, not an echo: it is a genuine bounded concurrency gate the swarm actually blocks on. 

Internals: an asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency) plus an in_use counter and a warm counter, guarded by an asyncio.Lock. acquire(slot_key, timeout): await asyncio.wait_for(self._sem.acquire(), timeout) — if more than max_concurrency workers try to enter, the (max+1)th genuinely SUSPENDS until a release() frees a permit (provably observable in tests: launch max+1 tasks, assert exactly max make progress and the last only proceeds after a release). On success increment in_use, return Slot(token=uuid, slot_key, backend='sim'). On timeout raise CapacityTimeout (same domain exception the real adapter raises — so the Service behaves identically). 

release(slot): idempotent (track released tokens in a set); decrement in_use, self._sem.release(). ensure_capacity(target): clamp and return min(target, max_concurrency) (pre-warm is free in-process — no-op but honest about the ceiling). capacity(): CapacitySnapshot(max, in_use, available=max-in_use, warm=0, mode='sim'). reconcile(): returns current in_use (in-process truth is authoritative; nothing to recover). aclose(): set closed flag so further acquires raise; drain semaphore. 

Because it shares the exact Slot/CapacitySnapshot/CapacityTimeout contract and real blocking semantics, the sim is a faithful test double for the real adapter and is also the production fallback when AWS_* creds are absent — giving genuine OOM/overload protection (directly mitigating the 'no concurrency cap' and 'threadpool starvation' High vulns) even with no cloud.
wiring:
Composition root: orchestrator/backstop/composition.py (DI container) reads BACKSTOP integration mode + AWS_* env. If real creds + cluster config present AND mode=real -> instantiate FargateConcurrencyGate with an injected aioboto3 ECS client; else -> SemaphoreConcurrencyGate(max_concurrency=BACKSTOP_MAX_CONCURRENCY). The chosen ConcurrencyGatePort instance is a process-wide SINGLETON registered in the container and injected into SwarmService. 

Primary invocation — swarm.py / SwarmService.run_appeal_batch(): the concurrent orchestrator currently fans out one asyncio task per appeal with no cap. Rewired: for each appeal, the worker coroutine does `async with self.gate.slot(slot_key=appeal.id) as slot: await self._run_appeal(appeal)`. The gate is acquired BEFORE the per-appeal PAVO/call.py loop begins and released in the context-manager exit (success or exception) — this replaces the leaky fire-and-forget pattern and enforces the global concurrency ceiling. Optionally SwarmService calls gate.ensure_capacity(target=len(batch)) once at batch start to pre-warm. 

Secondary wiring: (1) FastAPI lifespan startup calls gate.reconcile() to recover live slots after restart; shutdown calls gate.aclose() (fixes 'no graceful shutdown' + 'fire-and-forget tasks'). (2) The dashboard/status route and cost.py read gate.capacity() for the live concurrency meter and burst-cost estimate. (3) The triage worklist / batch-ingestion service consults gate.capacity().available to throttle how fast it enqueues 835/837 backlog appeals (backpressure into the NOW feature bucket). 

Layering respected: Controller (server.py route / WS handler) -> SwarmService (use-case) -> ConcurrencyGatePort -> {FargateConcurrencyGate | SemaphoreConcurrencyGate} adapter. The Service depends only on the port; adapters are injected by composition.py. The gate never sees PHI — it only receives the surrogate appeal id as slot_key.
